answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a nebula as the anchor of the cost. A knoll stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a plume holds...
